summary: The note reports on electrical failures and power outages in mass transit, focusing on a September 4, 2023 subway failure and an October 17, 2023 Los Angeles metro blackout. It gathers accounts from commuters, engineers, transit workers and a Department of Transportation specialist to show technical causes, human and financial impacts. It closes with infrastructure upgrades underway, such as New York's solar-powered subway stations, and how commuters are adapting.
one_line: Overview of September and October 2023 transit power outages, their causes, human and economic impacts, and infrastructure upgrades underway.
key_facts: On September 4, 2023, an electrical failure in the subway's power grid stopped trains mid-commute and stranded commuters underground.
Nurse Sarah Jenkins relies on the subway to reach the city hospital and missed essential work hours in an understaffed unit during the September 4 outage.

Engineer Michael Anderson said the September outage was triggered by an outdated transformer that couldn't handle the load, causing a cascade that shut down critical control systems and halted the whole network.
Anderson described the problem as "old equipment, insufficient upgrades, and a grid under immense pressure."
Linda Ortiz of the Department of Transportation said "our infrastructure is aging rapidly, and modernization isn't keeping pace with the needs of growing populations."
On October 17, 2023, a major blackout hit the Los Angeles metro and compromised communication with the city's airport shuttle services, causing missed flights and connections.
Tourist Zachary Lee said the October 17 shutdown left people with no information on the situation or when it would resolve.
Train operator Maria Gonzalez called the September outage "grueling" because she had to calm passengers with limited communication with the control center.
Technician James Harding said restoring power requires diagnosing the fault, manual repairs or replacements, and rigorous safety checks.
Businesses reported significant losses from disrupted supply chains and absent employees during the September and October incidents, and transit authorities offered refunds and alternative services.
Graphic designer Olivia Martinez missed a crucial client meeting because of the September blackout, since her primary client is accessible only via train.
New York has started an extensive program to upgrade its power systems, including solar panels at multiple subway stations.
Commuters are coping with carpooling, remote work, and flexible hours.
